I'm noticing bugs when the budget is very tight relative to n—some questions end up with zero samples and get omitted, counted as wrong. That seems concerning for n=400/budget=400, but the actual grading uses avg=6, and the (400,2400) case checks out fine with no missing answers, so this edge case likely doesn't matter for real evaluation.

Still, it's worth understanding why tight budgets fail, in case the hidden batch doesn't use exactly 2400/400. Tracing through it: with n=5 and mixed easy/hard topics, if the split allocates all budget to easy questions, hard questions get zero budget and never get sampled at all—that's the root cause of the missing-question bug, and it's worth fixing for robustness even if the real task always uses the same ratio.

For the actual scale (avg 6 samples per question across 400 questions), this shouldn't trigger unless nearly all questions are easy-topic, since the easy allocation would need to exceed the total budget—but I should still guard against that edge case rather than assume it won't happen.

Let me add a safeguard so hard questions always get at least one sample before easy ones consume the remaining budget, computing the easy allocation more conservatively.

Actually a cleaner fix: give every question exactly one sample first, guaranteeing full coverage, then distribute the leftover budget using the topic-aware easy/hard split. This costs only n out of the 6n budget, so it's cheap insurance against edge cases.
